package_info.package_manager: system (Linux distribution package managers, e.g., apt/yum/pacman)
package_info.package_versions: All versions prior to the fix commit 204c3393c4c90a29ed6bef64e43849536e863a86 (see vendor advisories for exact version numbers)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a critical logic flaw in its image handling code (PutSubImage), which allows a specially crafted XPM image to trigger an infinite recursion, leading to denial-of-service (DoS) or potential stack exhaustion. This is not intentional malware, but a vulnerability that can be exploited for DoS attacks.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a crafted XPM image is loaded and displayed via libX11/libXpm consumers)
execution_context.file_location: libX11 source code (PutSubImage function), triggered via applications like sxpm or any XPM image loader

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a crafted XPM image is loaded, the code recursively splits image rows for transmission, but due to a logic error, the recursion never progresses, causing infinite recursion and stack exhaustion, resulting in denial-of-service.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code is suspicious because it allows untrusted image data to control recursion depth, leading to unbounded stack usage and process crash.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal image processing code should robustly handle all input sizes and formats, ensuring recursion or iteration always makes forward progress and terminates. Here, a crafted image can cause infinite recursion.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Recursive image splitting is legitimate for large images, but must always guarantee progress and termination.
key_indicators: Recursion depth controlled by attacker-supplied image dimensions
No progress in recursion due to incorrect calculation (bits vs pixels)

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious XPM image with extremely large width and specific bits_per_pixel values to trigger the bug.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious image is loaded by a vulnerable application (e.g., sxpm, or any XPM image loader using libX11/libXpm).

attack_chain.action: Vulnerable application calls xpmCreatePixmapFromImage, which calls XPutImage, which calls PutSubImage with attacker-controlled parameters.
attack_chain.leads_to: PutSubImage enters infinite recursion due to logic flaw.

attack_chain.action: Process stack is exhausted, causing application crash (denial-of-service).
attack_chain.leads_to: Denial-of-service; application is unavailable until restarted.

behavioral_signatures: Unbounded recursion in image processing functions (PutSubImage) triggered by untrusted image files
Application crash or stack overflow when loading large or malformed XPM images
Repeated calls to PutSubImage with identical or near-identical parameters
file_indicators: XPM images with extremely large width (e.g., > 65536 pixels) and high bits_per_pixel values
Presence of crafted XPM files known to trigger CVE-2023-43786 (e.g., https://github.com/jfrog/jfrog-CVE-2023-43786-libX11_DoS/blob/main/cve-2023-43786.xpm)
network_indicators: N/A (no network activity required for exploitation; local file or clipboard image load is sufficient)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for application crashes or stack overflows in processes that load XPM images using libX11/libXpm. Scan for XPM files with suspiciously large width/height or bits_per_pixel values. Use static analysis to identify unpatched libX11 versions. Employ fuzzing or targeted test cases to trigger the bug in a controlled environment.
